findings.text: follow-on: finding_disposition's folded/exempted rendering is unguarded — tests/test_findings_read_by_path.py only ever asserts disposition "open" (:141, :175), so a regression that mis-rendered a fold or an exemption, or that broke the plan-record path (_plan_findings :130, _split_anchor :69) which no test builds a plan record for, would keep the suite green.

follow-on: the walk couples to review's private helpers _committed_record_at and _INCOMPLETE_RECORD_MARK rather than a public committed-reader, so renaming either in review.py would silently break the walk (the mark check would admit .incomplete- records and the read would return None and be skipped) with no test covering that edge.

follow-on: when no root/checkout-path is supplied, committed_review_root resolves the tree against the mounted checkout but the scope boundary is computed from root_path=None, so an absolute finding path inside the checkout is scoped artefact and contributes no recurrence in the default CLI/MCP invocation.
